newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close down on futures selling.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close down on futures selling.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed down slightly on Thursday after seesawing in a 100-point range throughout the day, chiefly due to futures-related trading activity, brokers said.
"The market fell this afternoon on futures related selling," said Jason Tang in institutional sales at South China Brokerage."

The Hang Seng Index closed off 18.81 points at 12,473.56, falling sharply from the day's high of 12,535.19 in the early afternoon. Turnover was very healthy at HK$7.12 billion, substantially up on Wednesday's HK$6.30 billion.

The October Hang Seng Index futures contract closed down 38 points at 12,462. Trade in the contract, which expires on October 30, totalled 16,508 contracts, compared with 18,000 contracts on Wednesday. Open interest remained relatively flat at 33,916 contracts.
Brokers also said fears of fund raising at the market's current high level helped bring the index down in the afternoon.
Brokers said the suspension of trade by Hong Kong and Shanghai Hotels in the afternoon sparked rumours the company may be considering a rights issue. The company declined to comment.
Technical indicators are showing some weakness, analysts warned.
Momentum indicators on both the weekly and the daily charts are turning down, although volume levels remain strong and suggest that demand is broad based, said one local technical analyst.
The finance sector led the market. Properties were little changed, while utilities again came under selling pressure.
International banking giant HSBC, which has been leading the market for most of the second half of the year, added HK$1.00 to HK$158.00, a new all time high.
Turnover in the counter was heavy at HK$603.89 million, about 8.5 percent of the market's total turnover.
In the property sector Henderson Land managed to buck the downtrend, putting on HK$0.50 to HK$70.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties added HK$0.25 to HK$86.50.
HongKong Telecom lost HK$0.20 to HK$13.70. Technical analysts see strong resistance at the HK$14.00 level. China Light lost HK$0.60 to HK36.10.
Swire Pacific lost HK$0.25 to close at HK$71.00.
